research_goal: Research the safest maintainable way to add platform notification settings and webhook dispatch for Slack, Discord, and Microsoft Teams.
coding_context: agent-platform Python CLI, self-documenting JSON configs, and integration helper modules.
source_value_provenance: Slack payload text field <- Slack official incoming webhook docs checked 2026-06-01.
Discord payload content field and allowed mention risk <- Discord Execute Webhook docs checked 2026-06-01.
Teams Workflows webhook preference and connector deprecation risk <- Microsoft Support and Microsoft Learn docs checked 2026-06-01.
HTTP POST implementation without extra dependency <- Python urllib.request official docs checked 2026-06-01.
CLI and config validation structure <- agent-platform/src/agent_platform/cli.py and governance/config_contract.py inspected 2026-06-01.
plan_evidence: Use environment-variable secret injection <- provider webhook URLs behave as credentials and repository config contract requires self-documenting settings.
Use Python standard library urllib <- no installation is required and simple JSON POST is sufficient for webhook delivery.
Add integrations package <- existing agent-platform folders separate planning, evaluation, governance, memory, and oss by capability.
Default dry-run <- avoids accidental external messages during tests and evaluations.
stack_version_constraints: Python 3.11+ local CLI execution; no external package required.
Slack, Discord, and Teams webhook APIs are external services and should be rechecked before changing payload behavior.
Teams Workflows payload behavior may vary by tenant and workflow template, so payload_style remains configurable.
issue_discussion_notes: Community results indicate Teams migration confusion, but official Microsoft docs control the implementation decision.
Webhook and urllib Q&A are treated as implementation risk signals only; provider official docs are authoritative.
community_signal_notes: Reddit and Stack Overflow activity are discovery signals for migration pain and common pitfalls, not standalone factual proof.
language_options: Python 3.11+ for local CLI, tests, config validation, and existing platform helper consistency.
TypeScript/Node for webhook tooling and richer typed integration packages.
selected_language: Python 3.11+ for local CLI, tests, config validation, and existing platform helper consistency.
language_decision_notes: Selected Python because agent-platform is already Python-first, tested with unittest, and can send JSON POST requests with the standard library.
Rejected TypeScript because this change is not frontend-adjacent and would add another runtime boundary.
code_reference_notes: Follow the existing pattern of dataclasses or pure functions, JSON inputs, CLI subcommands, and unittest coverage.
Keep provider-specific behavior deterministic and isolated in one module.
architecture_options: Capability package inside agent-platform with pure validation and dispatch functions plus CLI entry points.
Prompt-only workflow that tells agents how to send notifications manually.
Background notification service with queue, retry, and delivery store.
architecture_decision_notes: Selected capability package plus CLI because it is testable, small, and consistent with the platform's current modular monolith.
Rejected prompt-only workflow because it cannot guard secrets or payload shape deterministically.
Rejected background service because no queue or retry requirement exists yet.
architecture_tradeoff_notes: Theory sources favor explicit boundaries and documented interfaces; practitioner repository evidence favors small modules and unittest-backed CLI checks. Both converge on a small capability package for this scope.
folder_structure_options: Add src/agent_platform/integrations for external service integrations and configs/integrations for shared settings.
Place notification code under adapters because webhook providers are external endpoints.
Place notification code under ops because it supports operational reporting.
folder_structure_decision_notes: Selected integrations because notifications are external service integrations, not runtime adapters or planning/evaluation logic.
Keep config under configs/integrations so providers and secret policy are discoverable next to other platform settings.
folder_semantics_notes: src/agent_platform/integrations contains reusable external-provider integration helpers.
configs/integrations contains self-documenting settings for external platforms and secret indirection.
tests/test_notifications.py validates provider payload and policy behavior.
maintainability_notes: A single config and module reduce duplicated prompt-level webhook logic.
Environment-variable secret indirection avoids repeated config edits when tokens rotate.
Dry-run and sender injection keep tests deterministic and safe.
findings: Provider payloads differ enough to justify deterministic provider builders.
Teams connector deprecation makes Workflows webhook documentation necessary.
No external package is necessary for simple JSON webhook POST.
options: Python standard-library notifier with dry-run and env var secrets.
Install a provider SDK for Slack and custom code for Discord/Teams.
recommendation: Use a Python standard-library notifier, self-documenting config, environment-variable secrets, provider payload builders, and dry-run default.

post_research_answers.what_was_verified: Verified provider official webhook docs, Python standard library HTTP POST support, and existing repository CLI/config patterns.
post_research_answers.best_option: Python standard-library notifier with self-documenting config and environment-variable secret injection.
post_research_answers.why_this_option: It satisfies the user request without new dependencies, keeps secrets out of git, and fits the existing platform structure.
post_research_answers.alternatives_rejected: Provider SDK installation was rejected as unnecessary for simple webhook POST; prompt-only instructions were rejected because they cannot be tested; a background service was rejected as out of scope.
post_research_answers.implementation_impact: Add configs/integrations settings, src/agent_platform/integrations module, CLI commands, docs, tests, and history records.
post_research_answers.risks_and_unknowns: Teams Workflows payload compatibility can vary; real sending needs user-provided webhook URL and provider-side setup.
post_research_answers.validation_plan: Run notification unit tests, full unittest suite, config contract, check-notifications, notify dry-run, memory bootstrap, grounding, and work evaluation.
post_research_answers.reusable_knowledge: Capture provider docs and secret policy in notification config and docs for future platform events.
post_research_answers.next_action: Implement and verify the notification module, config, CLI, and docs.

risks_or_unknowns: Teams Workflows payload expectations may differ by setup.
No real notification send can be verified until the user supplies webhook environment variables.
Provider rate limits and retries are not implemented yet.
